head: 1b31e607608331b97f7f15427b0ec935e739a707
summary: Gemma 4 12B IT w4a16 served by vLLM 0.26 in WSL2; all Stage 1 contract items exercised over HTTP
result: All nine items pass. Weights 8.28 GiB, KV cache 11.79 GiB / 92403 tokens, TTFT 0.39 s, text 1.13 s, image 1.22 s, tool call 0.72 s, structured JSON 1.57 s. Speech untested; peak VRAM not measurable via nvidia-smi because vLLM preallocates 0.9 of the card.
decision: Endpoint is viable for Stage 1. Keep VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 and VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 under WSL. Take VRAM figures from the vLLM startup log, never from nvidia-smi.

head: 1b31e607608331b97f7f15427b0ec935e739a707
summary: Speech input verified on Gemma 4 12B IT w4a16 via the vLLM endpoint
result: 8.68 s stereo 24 kHz FLAC = 215 audio tokens; verbatim transcript correct in 1.19 s; language and speaker tone identified correctly. Synthetic tones remain unreliable: a 440 Hz sine is called laughter at temperature 0 while a sweep is described correctly.
decision: Audio is speech-oriented and usable as-is. Do not extrapolate audio quality to non-speech sound. The sample stays outside the repository; a committable speech fixture is still needed.

head: 1b31e607608331b97f7f15427b0ec935e739a707
summary: Stage 1 smoke script: repository code drives every contract item against the local Gemma 4 endpoint
result: 9 of 9 checks pass with content assertions, not just status codes: text 0.27 s, system prompt 0.08 s, streaming 0.38 s (TTFT 0.04 s, 20 chunks), single image 0.12 s, two images 0.22 s, speech wav 0.25 s, speech flac 0.22 s, tool call 0.37 s, structured JSON 0.65 s. 42 offline tests pass without a server. Three first-run failures were real: unbounded numeric fields make guided decoding repeat digits until max_tokens is exhausted (fixed by minimum/maximum, 8.63 s unparsable -> 0.65 s correct); a 20 ms tone let a liveness check pass while the model received no audio; a (220,20,20) circle is called pink.
decision: Stage 1 closes. Every JSON schema this project sends must bound its numeric fields. Audio fixtures must carry speech, not synthetic tone.

head: 14036d0a38f68be80d42e382dbc6855f22ebc09f
summary: Can LangGraph be used without adopting LangChain types? Measured against langgraph 1.2.10 in a throwaway environment.
result: Core StateGraph ran a two-iteration tool loop on the project's own frozen dataclasses and restored 4 messages for a thread from InMemorySaver; langgraph.types.interrupt is present for confirmation gates. The prebuilts refuse: create_react_agent's signature requires a langchain_core BaseChatModel or Runnable, and ToolNode inside a graph accepted a langchain_core AIMessage but rejected the project's dataclass with NotImplementedError: Unsupported message type. langgraph 1.2.10 depends on langchain-core<2,>=1.4.7 regardless, so langchain_core is installed either way. One caveat found: checkpointing unregistered custom classes warns 'this will be blocked in a future version', so graph state should hold JSON-able structures or register its types.
decision: Use LangGraph core with the project's own message type; write the tool loop by hand. Do not use create_react_agent or ToolNode. See DECISIONS.md 2026-08-01.

head: 4c5663ab42a3e4ce4f40bfc2eebcf3da4d914822
summary: The tool loop closes: a two-node LangGraph graph drives a real call-tool-answer cycle on the project's own Message type
result: Live run against gemma-4-12b-it on vLLM: the model chose list_files{path=.}, then read_file{path=README.md}, then answered from the file contents. Two tool iterations, seven messages, 3.82 s end to end. vLLM accepted an assistant turn with content null plus tool_calls, and the tool-role replies carrying tool_call_id. Offline: 72 tests pass, 30 of them new.
decision: Assistant turns serialize with content null when they only call tools. Tool failures are returned to the model as tool messages rather than raised, so a mistyped path costs a turn instead of the run. Loop bounding is left to LangGraph's recursion limit; no counter in the graph.

head: 3600757d3e99773722224e55f7efc90547e2ef70
summary: Stage 2: four-node LangGraph agent with tools, SQLite memory and a rolling summary, run live against vLLM
result: Two sessions in one run, 10.0 s for eight model calls: remember_fact and list_files in session one, search_memory in a new thread after reopening the store, summary written covering positions 0-11 with all 18 messages still stored. 137 offline tests pass.
decision: Stage 2 closed; Stage 3 grows the same graph with checkpoints and interrupt rather than replacing it

head: a0c92af5d93d5ec8029c32a79abf6d1ee76c3374
summary: Stage 3 first step: checkpoints, resumable turns, and confirmation before a destructive tool
result: Live: the model called write_file, the turn stopped with nothing written, the agent was closed and reopened, the same question came back with its id and arguments intact, approving wrote the file and declining left it alone with the refusal reaching the model. Whole flow 4.0 s. 156 offline tests pass, up from 137.
decision: A tool declares itself destructive and the graph asks; without a checkpointer there is nowhere to wait, so the call is declined rather than run

head: 012a3d997eec713166365eb77a466008f732d642
summary: Version 1 live check against vLLM: token budget from the server, a fold triggered by measured request size, the thread list, and a dead endpoint
result: context_limit 16384 from /v1/models, budget 9830 at fraction 0.6; one real turn 470/9830 tokens in 0.5 s; at fraction 0.02 (budget 327) three short turns used 468/483/513 tokens and folded through 0 -> 2 -> 4 with a readable summary and no message lost; two threads listed with their openings; a dead endpoint cost 3 attempts and 6.3 s and named itself
decision: Version 1 closes. Keep the fold reactive and the fraction at 0.6: the turn that overshoots still fits and the fold happens before the next one.
